recipes.name: Double Cheesy Au Gratin Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 4 large baking potatoes, peeled and sliced thin

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 2 quart baking dish.
Layer potato slices in prepared baking dish. Pour cream over potatoes; sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Season potatoes with salt and pepper.
Bake in preheated oven until potatoes are soft, about 1 hour. Remove from oven; gently stir potatoes. Sprinkle with the Cheddar cheese; cover and let rest until cheese is melted, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Double Cheesy Au Gratin Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: Tender potatoes, rich cream, and two cheeses bake up into one fantastic au gratin potato dish.

review.reviewBody: SO rich and cheesy! I used a cup of heavy cream and a cup of 1% milk, and added a couple of small pats of butter to the mix before I baked it and it came out perfectly. We devoured this with some steak tips and were stuffed!!!

I make this without the cheddar; adding horseradish & an apple; & different directions. So high in fat, but everyone likes it. 'Mix together & pour over the potatoes (& a peeled, sliced granny smith apple in the middle layer): 3 1/2c heavy cream, 1/3c horseradish (not to worry, it mellows as it cooks :D), 1/2t salt & 1/2t freshly ground pepper. I place a sheet of foil loosely over a 9x13 then remove it after half an hour. Bake another half hour & then add the parmesan on top while the oven is off, but hot. No stirring. Let it sit in the oven ten minutes or even longer to thicken. Oh, yeah, I bake mine at 400. If I were using a casserole dish, I'd probably go for 350; but I don't know if they'd be as good without sitting in the cream completely as they cook.

This was an excellent guide, and turned out great. I made a lot of changes just because I like everything extra! I kept the amounts the same but left out onions. I added bacon bits and 3 tablespoons of fresh parsley, a teaspoon of oregano and a half tsp. Of paprika and instead of cheddar, I used a cup of shredded Parmesan and half a cup of a mix of shredded Mexican blend and Mexican velveeta. After baking it 15 mins longer than the recipe calls for, I topped it with about 1/3 cup of cheddar and then finely grated seasoned croutons, then baked another 15 mins until slightly golden for a crispy crust on top which balances perfectly with the creamy seasonings inside. It turned out better than any au gratin I’d ever made before and he fell in love with me all over again.

Delicious with some modifications. I was concerned with the enormous fat/calorie content, so opted to use fat free half and half and cut down the quantity considerably (about 2 cups) Instead, I heated the half and half with a little butter and then added the cheddar cheese to make a sauce. Slowly cooked until thick. I made layers (potatoes, parm, repeat) and then poured the thickened sauce over. Topped with bread crumbs. Cooked at 375 for about an hour - topped with tinfoil for the first 40 min and removed for the remaining time to get the top layer a little more crunchy. Turned out pretty well!

I don't think you can go wrong with these ingredients. But I am sorry I had to scale it back. First off I did not need a full quart of cream, used under just 2 cups and about 1/2 cup chicken broth. Second, all I needed to do is layer this, add potatoes sprinkle with parm and butter, some cream and broth and dot with butter, sprinkle with cheddar and repeat layers, I had 3 layers. This is so good I used a mandolin to get potatoes really thin. I will be making this again and again, thanks.

I made this tonight for dinner with my son and his new girlfriend. I did make a couple of changes to suit my taste. I used half &half instead of heavy cream, and I added salt, pepper to each layer instead of just the last layer. I also added a few thin slices of butter to each layer. I agree with another reviewer about the cook time. At 350/1 hour, the potatoes weren't quite done. But, I just put it in a larger casserole dish, and since I was baking chicken too, I upped the temp to 400 degrees F. Regardless of the fact that the rest of the meal was done before the potatoes, it was worth the extra wait. His girlfriend LOVED the meal, especially the potatoes. She even asked me for the recipe. I guess I made a good first impression.

I scaled this back to suit two people tonight using russet potatoes. I also used half-n- half milk with a pad of butter. Preparing this was easy as was baking it in the oven. I seasoned the potatoes with black pepper and Hawaiian sea salt; layered the potatoes with more fresh shredded parmesan and less sharp cheddar cheese in the gratin dish and then poured the cream over the top. I placed the butter on top and baked as recipe instructed for one hour. This turned out to be a nice rich sauce with cheesy potatoes! This is definitely not “diet” food but a great side dish for our ham tonight. I served this with, “Creamy Sweet Corn,” and “Glazed Ham,” also from this website. Very tasty.
I used a mixture of parmesan cheese and bread crumbs for the topping,along with pads of butter. Placed aluminum foil on dish. Took off for the final 10 minutes. Also added garlic to spices.

I made these to go with our Sunday dinner. They were so good! I was cooking a few other things, so I put these in the crockpot. I layered the potatoes, along with thinly sliced onion, and minced garlic, sea salt & pepper. I topped with heavy cream and parmesan cheese. Once the potatoes were done, I topped with cheddar cheese. I was going to take a picture, but they were gone before I could:) I will certainly be making again. Thanks for sharing!

Very good, but I added seasoned salt and lots of garlic powder. Instead of using a whole quart of cream, I used one cup of cream and one cup of 2% milk. I also added a few tablespoons of butter. The next time we make it, we will add diced poblano peppers. That will really add some nice flavor.
This a great recipe! My family loved it. I made it for Christmas dinner. When I layered in the potatoes I added a half cup of parmesan cheese to each layer. Was fantastic.
Previous review i forgot to add that i doubled the recipe. Maybe the cream shouldn't be doubled.
Made this with 1 C heavy cream and 1 C 1% milk and added a few dollops of butter and it was fantastic! Will make again and again!
Delicious, I made it for myself. Once my family got tastes of it they devoured it. I make it once a month now as a comfort food.
I added bacon and made this for our potato dish on Thanksgiving....everyone loved it!
I reduced the amount of cream and still found there was far too much liquid. The cream seperated and I found them quite flavourless. It didn't look very appealing when it came out of the oven.
Bland and very runny.
Good fast and almost healthy.
Easy to reduce recipe
Taste was good, but SOOOO soupy! Next time I will cut down on the liquid. Even Velveeta added in didn't help.
